questions.q: What has to exist before a table has a working Table API endpoint?
options: Nothing extra — every table gets one automatically the moment the table exists
A sys_ws_definition record pointing at that table
A Resource record with a custom script for each HTTP method
A manually written GlideRecord wrapper script
questions.explain: The Table API is automatic and built-in — no sys_ws_definition, Resource, or script is required for it to work.

questions.q: GET /api/now/table/incident/{sys_id} returns what, compared to GET /api/now/table/incident with no sys_id?
options: A list of every incident the caller can see, unfiltered
Exactly one incident record, the one matching that sys_id
Nothing — a sys_id is only valid on POST requests
A count of incidents only, with no field data
questions.explain: Including a sys_id in the path always means "give me exactly one record"; omitting it means "give me a list."

questions.q: GET /api/now/table/incident?sysparm_query=active=true^priority=1 — what does the ^ do in sysparm_query?
options: It joins the two conditions with AND, the same as an encoded query built with GlideRecord
It escapes the = character so it isn't treated as part of the URL
It tells the Table API to return results in descending order
It marks the field name as case-insensitive
questions.explain: sysparm_query accepts the same encoded-query syntax GlideRecord.addQuery() produces, where ^ chains conditions with AND.

questions.q: In a list GET with &sysparm_fields=number,short_description&sysparm_limit=25, what does sysparm_fields control versus sysparm_limit?
options: sysparm_fields controls which fields appear in each returned record; sysparm_limit caps how many records come back
sysparm_fields caps how many records come back; sysparm_limit controls which fields appear
They do the same thing and either one alone has the same effect
sysparm_fields sorts the results; sysparm_limit filters which table is queried
questions.explain: sysparm_fields trims the fields serialized per record; sysparm_limit caps the number of records in the response.

questions.q: A team needs to combine data from two related tables into one custom-shaped response field before sending it to an external system. Why is the Table API the wrong tool here?
options: The Table API always returns a table's raw field structure from a single table — it can't combine tables or reshape a response, which is exactly what a Scripted REST API is for
The Table API cannot accept any query parameters at all
The Table API only supports the DELETE method
The Table API cannot be used with sysparm_query under any circumstances
questions.explain: The Table API mirrors one table's fields with no custom logic in between — combining tables or reshaping output requires a Scripted REST API.
